info.name: Reports - FDA dashboard, sales and pharmacy doctors
info.description:
# FDA dashboard and pharmacy doctors

All saved responses are illustrative synthetic examples, not captured production results.

## Authentication and environments
Header `API-KEY: {{api_key}}`; query parameters `token` and `requester`. Enter your own credentials after import.
UAT: https://zuat-accounting-back.myt-emr.com
Production: https://accounting-back.myt-emr.com
Set `base_url` to the environment you intend to read. This collection contains GET requests only.

## Branches and IDs
1 Mobile; 2 Oakridge; 3 Mactan; 4 Consolacion; 7 Mantlewood.
Doctor `id` is pharmacy_doctor.id, not doctor_id. IDs are local to each branch: keep branch_id together with id. Identical doctor names or IDs in different branches are separate records.

## FDA dashboard
GET /reports/get_fda_dashboard
Optional branch_id: omit or leave empty for all available branches.
Optional pharmacy_doctor_id: one positive integer; requires branch_id. Filters dispense_medicine_details.pharmacy_doctor_id, so different doctors on the same dispensing header are filtered independently.
Optional date_from/date_to: supply both as valid YYYY-MM-DD dates; inclusive filtering on medicine-detail added_on. Existing date handling is retained; use date_from <= date_to for a meaningful range.
Optional patient_id/item_id: single numeric IDs; existing branch-local behavior is retained.
Optional term: searches patient_name, doctor_name and generic.
Pagination: page (default 1), data_size (default 20); page_size remains an alias when data_size is omitted.
Order: numeric rx_no ascending, then branch_id ascending, before pagination. rx_no remains the medicine-detail ID; it is not the dispensing-header number.
Response: data, size (full filtered count), page, data_size, total_pages. Existing row fields are unchanged.
When a branch lacks the pharmacy_doctor_id source column, a doctor-filtered FDA result is empty for that branch; the filter is never ignored. Unknown positive doctor IDs also return no matching rows.

## Pharmacy-doctor lookup
GET /reports/get_pharmacy_doctor
Optional branch_id: omit/empty for all supported branches. Returns all matching non-deleted doctors without pagination, ordered by name, branch_id, id.
The master connection checks pharmacy_doctor table existence in the configured diagnostic schemas before querying. Missing tables are skipped. Real metadata/data query failures are errors, not empty successes.
Response: data and size. Each doctor retains id, doctor_id, name, lic_no, is_cpci, audit/deletion fields, plus source branch_id/branch_name. No deduplication across branches; leading-zero license numbers remain strings. No doctors or no available tables returns {"data": [], "size": 0}.

## Workflow
1. Read the doctor list for all branches or a selected branch.
2. Copy the selected row's id into pharmacy_doctor_id and its branch_id into branch_id.
3. Send the selected-branch/doctor FDA request.
Disabled query parameters can be enabled in Postman; clear unused filter values.

## FDA sales (local implementation only)
GET /reports/get_fda_sales
Uses existing authenticated report access. This new endpoint is local only; no UAT/production deployment is included. Existing dashboard and pharmacy-doctor requests remain unchanged.
Groups active dispense_medicine_details by branch, added_by, item_id and DATE(added_on). Branch-local user/item IDs never merge across branches. Omitted/blank branch_id merges available diagnostic sources 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 through the master connection; a selected branch reads only that source. Missing dispensing tables are skipped, but incompatible required columns and real query failures remain errors.
Optional filters: branch_id, paired date_from/date_to (inclusive YYYY-MM-DD calendar days), patient_id, item_id, term, brand, generic, dosage, form, kind, page and data_size. IDs/page sizes must be positive integers; branch must be supported. Supply both dates or neither; reversed ranges and invalid dates return HTTP 400. Text filters accept strings or null, trim surrounding whitespace, and skip blank values; string "0" is a real filter.
term uses case-insensitive substring LIKE matching across branch-local item.name, the branch-local user's full name, and saved detail doctor_name/patient_name. Normal SQL LIKE wildcards remain supported. brand/generic/dosage/form compare the current branch item catalog exactly, not historical detail snapshots. kind uses comma-separated complete-token OR matching. Different filters combine using AND. All filters apply before sums and CSV assembly, so patient/name filters can reduce a group's totals and CSV values.
quantity, price and amount are independent SUM values, with null numeric inputs treated as zero. price is the sum of the saved prices, not an average or a price multiplied by quantity. These sums are returned as decimal strings without PHP floating-point rounding. added_by/item_id remain scalar; added_on is the calendar day YYYY-MM-DD. Rows also include branch_id/name, item_name and dispense_by_name. Dispenser names come only from user in that source schema (first, middle and last name, skipping blank components). Missing item/user metadata returns null names without removing otherwise valid sales. Soft-deleted detail rows are excluded when is_deleted exists; existing user/item records can still name historical sales.
Every remaining detail column is returned as a CSV string of distinct nonblank values, ordered by first contributing detail ID. This includes detail id, dispensing-header IDs, patient/doctor IDs, saved names/medication attributes and audit fields when present. Null-only/blank-only or source-unavailable columns return null. "0", case and leading zeros are preserved. CSV quotes fields as needed, including embedded commas, quotes, whitespace and line breaks; parse each CSV field with a CSV parser, not a plain split(','). Each column is independently distinct; positions across different CSV columns do not imply a row relationship. Source-specific optional fields may extend the returned columns. Derived branch/name fields and scalar grouping/sum fields retain their documented meanings.
Grouped totals and counts are calculated in SQL. CSV assembly reads contributing details in batches for only the selected page, avoiding GROUP_CONCAT truncation. Results return {data,size,page,data_size,total_pages}, ordered by day ASC, branch_id ASC, added_by ASC, item_id ASC. size counts groups before pagination; defaults are page 1/data_size 20. The Core page_size alias is accepted when data_size is omitted and must also be positive. Empty results return HTTP 200 with data=[], size=0 and total_pages=0. A page beyond the last page keeps the matching size and returns data=[].
Saved sales examples are illustrative synthetic, abridged detail projections. No real patients, users or production results are included. No request execution scripts, writes or automatic retries are added.
